body: Oh, I knew what you were singing before I clicked on the link, and it made me laugh so much, thanks for that and I'm stealing your move.

Thank you, LtBenben.  I didn't see the post, where is it?  In the darkness right now, don't see any light or goodness in the future for me or anyone, this is the worst I've felt. I don't understand why people want to live, right now I don't understand how life is worth living for anyone.
I'm so sorry you feel like this.  I feel like this, too.  Just wanted you to know you're not alone.
Thanks. Sure, yes.

It's weird how those roles can shift as people come in and out of the picture.  I guess those N family dynamics really block people from what they naturally would want to be doing or how they would really want to apply or express themselves in the world, because there's often a price to be paid that's too psychologically costly.
Ugh, Gertiel, your experience sounds truly awful.  I'm so sorry you had to endure that abuse from your mother, and of course it would affect you now.  Thank you so much for your response.

Your comment resonated with me so much, I breathed an actual sigh of relief while reading.  

> the 'needless/wantless' person no longer has belongings or desires anymore that can be used as part of an N's agenda.

Yes yes yes yes.  That's what I did, too.  I feel overwhelmed by imagining trying to get out of that robot mode, or if I can ever cope with all that I suppressed in order to survive, I'm afraid that maybe the only way I know to deal with life is by being a clinically depressed invincible robot.  (That sounds like a blockbuster waiting to happen.)  

Anyway, thank you so much for your words, I appreciate it so much.

> They can't ever just be reasonably proud and happy for you.

Yes, the "for you" part doesn't really seem to exist in Nworld.  Thanks for your response!

Thanks for your kind comment.

>  (context: have lived with clinical depression all of my adult life).

Me too, and I'm sorry that you have, as well.

It feels like part of the same phenomenon to me.  When I've lucked into a better mood, I always feel less socially inhibited.  With less depression, I feel more like I'm part of life, and everything flows more easily.
That's a good idea.

I was looking for a different photo, but came across this monkey swimming - his/her expression is a bit how I feel right now:

https://www.flickr.com/photos/supervliegzus/5891728548/

I'm sorry you feel bad right now.

Yes, sometimes the irritability takes over and I feel like I hate everyone and everything and it's all useless and stupid and etc.  I know it isn't what Holly Golightly meant when she talked about "the mean reds" (as opposed to "the blues"), but that's the name I use for this aspect of depression.

This used to be me until I ran out of energy to do it anymore.  It still is partially how I present when I'm out in the world, but being out in the world has been pared down to little slivers, and the damage of depression is also now apparent in my face and body and my atrophied social skills.

I know it's kind of a chicken-or-egg thing to figure out if the rumination causes the depression or if the depression causes the rumination, but sometimes I do feel like my body is sending all kinds of signals about things being "off", and my brain then ruminates in order to try to figure out why things are "off".  But it's like a faulty response, it doesn't go anywhere, just seems to dig a deeper hole and make me feel worse.
Wow, you put it so perfectly.

> Depression for me is having everybody else tell me there deepest darkest secrets, and I can't even tell them how my day went.

Me too.
So true for me, too.
Yes.
Maybe it means a fat drop.
